paragraphs: One-sentence assessment | This career is worth exploring further only if you are willing to undertake lengthy doctoral education in psychology, an internship and two years of postdoctoral specialty training; can maintain accurate test administration and scoring for extended periods under standardized conditions; are willing to turn cognitive and behavioral performance into clinical reports that can be reviewed and explicitly state uncertainty; and can respect your professional boundaries when making high-stakes judgments involving neurological disease.

Core output | Turn the referral question, medical history, standardized test profile, informant information and behavioral observations into a traceable clinical neuropsychological report: descriptive or diagnostic conclusions, explanations of cognitive strengths and weaknesses, differential considerations, recommendations and referrals, rather than just a set of scores.

20—120-minute safe trial | Conduct a nonclinical exercise using a fictional case: specify the referral question and key history, select three tests matching your hypotheses from public test descriptions and explain your reasons, then write two paragraphs of feedback for family members. Do not use this exercise to diagnose, score or recommend treatment for any real individual.

First hurdle | Verify qualifications and boundaries first: who may administer and interpret neuropsychological tests, make diagnoses and sign reports. The United States requires state psychologist licensure, including the EPPP and supervised hours; neuropsychology board certification (ABPP/ABCN) is a voluntary professional credential. In mainland China, psychotherapy must take place in medical institutions and be provided by licensed psychiatrists or assistant psychiatrists, or health professionals qualified through the national health professional technical qualification examination in psychotherapy. Specific assessment permissions follow current regulations and institutional policies.

entries: History and interviews | Interview patients and informants to obtain a comprehensive history, course of illness and past history, and clarify the current referral question and clinical questions to be answered.

Standardized assessment | Select and administer standardized tests of intelligence, academic abilities, attention and concentration, sensorimotor function, language, learning and memory, following uniform administration and scoring conditions.

Report writing | Write detailed clinical neuropsychological reports using tests, self-report measures, rating scales, direct observations and interview data, explaining the strength and limitations of the evidence.

Diagnosis and treatment | Diagnose and treat conditions involving central nervous system damage, such as cerebrovascular accidents, tumors, infectious or inflammatory diseases, degenerative diseases, traumatic brain injuries, demyelinating diseases and various dementias.
Baseline and follow-up | Establish neurobehavioral baseline measurements to monitor functional changes during progressive brain disease or rehabilitation.

Education, consultation and supervision | Provide education or counseling to individuals and families, consult with other professionals about patients' neurological conditions, and educate and supervise interns and staff.

paragraphs: The core capability of neuropsychologists is turning cognitive and behavioral performance into interpretable evidence: collecting history systematically, administering and scoring tests correctly, interpreting profiles alongside informant information and behavioral observations, producing reports useful to referring professionals, and explaining the strength and limitations of conclusions in interprofessional communication.

Work primarily involves assessments in outpatient clinics, inpatient wards and rehabilitation facilities, almost entirely indoors. O*NET work context data show that 96% work indoors in environmentally controlled conditions daily; 60% have face-to-face discussions daily and 32% several times a week; 80% work more than 40 hours per week, and 96% have regular schedules.

Decision-making autonomy is relatively high, but consequences vary considerably: O*NET shows that 76% report substantial freedom to make decisions and 72% consider exactness or accuracy extremely important. Responses on the consequences of errors range from "very serious" at 16% and "serious" at 20% to "not serious at all" at 24%, indicating that risk varies with the purpose of assessment and population.

The emphasis is on interpreting and integrating evidence, beyond the mechanics of test administration: placing test scores, behavioral observations, history and informant information within a single interpretive framework, and explaining which conclusions are supported by evidence and which remain hypotheses requiring verification.

Quality is measured by traceable assessment conditions, justified scoring and normative reference selection, interpretation aligned with the referral question, clear statements of report limitations, and usable follow-up baselines and recommendations, rather than the number of tests or report length.

Responsibility boundaries | Diagnosis, test interpretation and report signing must be undertaken by appropriately qualified practitioners working within their authorized scope. Psychometrists, research assistants and interns may administer tests and record information, but do not make diagnostic conclusions or sign reports. In mainland China, psychotherapy must be delivered in medical institutions by eligible personnel; specific neuropsychological assessment permissions follow current regulations and institutional policies.

The workflow proceeds as follows: clarify the referral question and informed consent → collect history and informant information → select and administer standardized tests → score, integrate and interpret findings to form descriptive or diagnostic conclusions → write the report and provide feedback → make recommendations and referrals and conduct follow-up testing. Occupational boundaries | This occupation is distinct from neurologists, who make medical diagnoses and prescribe medications; clinical psychologists, who provide general psychological assessment and therapy; and neurodiagnostic technologists, who perform examinations and organize technical data. This occupation does not make medical diagnoses or prescribe medications.

Neurologists | Medically diagnose and treat diseases of the brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerves, may prescribe medications and interpret imaging, and provide long-term medication management for nonsurgical neurological conditions. This occupation centers on standardized cognitive and behavioral assessments and reports, without prescribing medications.

Clinical psychologists | Provide general psychological assessment and psychotherapy and typically do not conduct systematic neuropsychological assessments. Neurodiagnostic technologists perform examinations such as electroencephalography and organize technical data, without making diagnoses or signing reports. Adjacent classifications do not make qualifications or permissions interchangeable.

Selection signal | Compare more than the fact that these occupations all assess psychological or brain-related functioning. Consider who makes diagnoses, whether they issue neuropsychological reports, whether they have prescribing and medical treatment authority, and whether entry requires a psychology doctorate plus postdoctoral specialty training or a medical degree plus residency training.

Centers on medical diagnosis and medication treatment, with authority to prescribe medications and interpret imaging, and responsibility for long-term medical management of neurological diseases. This occupation centers on assessment profiles, descriptive or diagnostic conclusions and reports.

Consider this occupation if you want standardized assessment, reports and cognitive rehabilitation recommendations to be your main work and are willing to complete a psychology doctorate and two years of postdoctoral specialty training. Consider neurology if you prefer responsibility for medical diagnosis, treatment and prescribing.

Potential assistance (editorial analysis): authorized history summaries, report formatting and checklist checks, and drafts of educational materials. Test lists and scoring checks must be handled in licensed systems. This review did not obtain evidence of accuracy or clinical outcomes.

Search queries and candidate public references may serve as drafts. Humans must verify test versions, normative populations and evidence strength. Do not provide nonpublic test items, responses or normative materials to unlicensed models.

Risk-screening assistance | May flag missing fields, inconsistencies or items requiring retesting; cannot replace original responses, administration conditions, behavioral observations or clinical judgment.

Do not delegate to AI | Making diagnostic or descriptive conclusions, interpreting test profiles, selecting norms, writing final report conclusions, recommending treatment or medications, or handling informed consent and privacy decisions.

Human control points | Verify the examinee's identity and informed consent, confirm administration conditions and scoring, and interpret the sources of abnormalities: the test, the person's state or functioning. A qualified practitioner must sign the report and address urgent risks.

Data requirements | Process only the minimum necessary information in authorized systems. Test materials, responses and reports must not be entered into unauthorized external models or tools, and institutional privacy and ethics rules must be followed.

Capability development | Build skills in structured history taking, accurate administration and scoring, profile interpretation, interprofessional communication and report writing, rather than merely generating text faster.

This occupation corresponds to the US O*NET19-3039.02. This review did not verify a one-to-one mapping to Chinese classifications or practice qualifications. Article 51 of the Mental Health Law requires psychotherapy to take place in medical institutions; personnel specializing in psychotherapy may not diagnose mental disorders, prescribe medications or perform surgery. This does not negate the diagnostic and treatment authority of qualified psychiatrists. The 2013 standards permit psychotherapy by licensed psychiatrists or assistant psychiatrists who have completed standardized psychotherapy training, or personnel who have passed the health qualification examination in psychotherapy. This alone does not confer all neuropsychological assessment permissions.

paragraphs: Caution signal (editorial observation): an interest in studying the brain also requires investment in relevant psychology education, supervised training, documentation and ongoing learning. Two postdoctoral years are an ABCN certification requirement for specific training cohorts and should not be generalized to all countries, positions or research roles.

Verification method | Personality and interest labels cannot determine fit. Use a fictional case to practice test selection and profile interpretation, and obtain evaluation from qualified clinicians in a compliant teaching environment.

Scope statement | This checklist cannot replace institutional clinical protocols, ethical requirements for test use, or privacy and safety requirements. Major risks include inappropriate test and norm selection, deviations in administration conditions and scoring, overinterpretation of profiles, overlooked validity and motivation factors, and failure to escalate high-risk findings promptly. Controls should be tailored to the institution and scope of practice.

Direct answer | The main risks are inappropriate test and norm selection, errors in scoring or administration conditions, treating scores as diagnoses themselves, overlooking validity and motivation factors, underestimating the cognitive effects of depression, pain, medication or sleep, and failing to escalate according to protocol when risks of self-harm, harm to others or acute neurological events are identified.

Evidence scope: O*NET figures for accuracy at 72%, decision-making freedom at 76% and the distribution of error consequences support the work context, without establishing risk incidence or the reasons for differences. ABCN training requirements do not establish control effectiveness. Controls are editorial recommendations to be tailored by institutions. Chinese law and the 2013 standards apply only to Chinese entities and the scope of psychotherapy.

Affected roles | Neuropsychologists responsible for selecting and administering tests, scoring and interpreting profiles, and writing and signing reports, as well as interns and psychometrists working under their supervision. Referring professionals' reliance on reports can amplify the impact of incorrect conclusions.

Possible consequences | Incorrect conclusions may misdirect diagnosis and care, lead to unnecessary examinations or miss treatable causes. Overlooking validity and motivation factors may turn test bias into an apparent functional impairment. Missing records and statements of limitations can prevent conclusions from being reviewed and accountability from being established.

Step 0: determine the practice jurisdiction and authorized scope | First identify the country or region where you plan to practice, and verify requirements for doctoral psychology education, internship, postdoctoral training, licensure and specialty certification. The pathway on this page is an editorial synthesis, does not represent uniform entry requirements and does not authorize any assessment, diagnosis, test interpretation or report signing.

Study psychology and clinical foundations, neuroanatomy and brain–behavior relationships, and psychometric foundations in a supervised setting, and complete doctoral internship and assessment work under supervision.
Doctoral education and internship stage

Complete the supervised internship required by the applicable licensing rules and program. ABCN prefers APA/CPA-accredited internships, but its general review may accept other internship credentials and does not require neuropsychology training during the internship. Verify specific credential review and institutional authorization separately.
Doctoral internship and neuropsychology training

ABCN certification requirements vary by the completion date of doctoral training or respecialization. For completion on or after 2005-01-01, postdoctoral training equivalent to two full-time years, scheduled at least half-time, is required. At least 50% of postdoctoral training must involve supervised clinical neuropsychological services; specific supplementary guidelines require at least 50% of those clinical services to involve integrative assessment. The overview also states that services must be integrative. Verify these requirements through application review; they cannot be reduced to a uniform duration for every position.
Postdoctoral specialty training

After obtaining the applicable jurisdictional license, institutional privileges and required specialty competence, undertake assessments and reporting within your authorized scope. ABPP/ABCN professional certification is distinct from legal licensure; verify certification requirements with the employer and institution.

entries.answer: In the United States, state psychologist licensure is the legal prerequisite for independent practice, typically requiring doctoral education, supervised hours and passing the EPPP. ABPP/ABCN clinical neuropsychology specialty certification is a voluntary professional credential, with a requirement to adopt Houston Conference training standards from January 1, 2005, but does not replace licensure or institutional authorization. In mainland China, psychotherapy providers must be licensed psychiatrists or assistant psychiatrists, or health professionals qualified through the health professional technical qualification examination in psychotherapy. Psychotherapy must take place in medical institutions.

entries.answer: The usual neuropsychology pathway involves a psychology doctorate and two years of postdoctoral training, making career transition costly. A low-cost first step is to use public test descriptions and a fictional case for an exercise in "test selection + profile interpretation + report outline" to assess your willingness to undertake standardized testing and writing over the long term. Then verify education, internship and licensing requirements with the target institutions and jurisdiction. The exercise does not authorize diagnosis or practice and cannot replace any legally required qualification.

locale_requirements.summary: ABCN certification requirements vary by the completion date of doctoral training or respecialization. For completion on or after 2005-01-01, postdoctoral training equivalent to two full-time years, scheduled at least half-time, is required. At least 50% of postdoctoral training must involve supervised clinical neuropsychological services; specific supplementary guidelines require at least 50% of those clinical services to involve integrative assessment. The overview also states that services must be integrative. Verify these requirements through application review; they cannot be reduced to a uniform duration for every position. components.definition_block: Neuropsychologists (O*NET-SOC 19-3039.02) center their work on standardized assessment and clinical reports: interviewing and taking histories, administering neuropsychological tests and scales, integrating observations and informant information to interpret cognitive, emotional and behavioral performance, diagnosing and treating conditions associated with central nervous system damage, and establishing follow-up baselines. Actual permitted activities depend on psychologist licensure, institutional authorization and jurisdictional rules. The occupational title itself does not confer physician status or prescribing authority. Diagnosis, treatment and report signing each require verification of jurisdictional licensure and institutional permissions; psychotherapy and neuropsychological assessment do not map one-to-one to Chinese qualifications.

questions.answer: In the United States, state psychologist licensure is the legal prerequisite; ABPP/ABCN clinical neuropsychology specialty certification is a voluntary professional credential. questions.answer: People without a psychology background cannot independently assess others on interest alone, but may complete the required education and supervised training. Support roles also require verification of authorization; it cannot be asserted that they must remain in support roles permanently.

questions.answer: ABCN certification requirements vary by the completion date of doctoral training or respecialization. For completion on or after 2005-01-01, postdoctoral training equivalent to two full-time years, scheduled at least half-time, is required. At least 50% of postdoctoral training must involve supervised clinical neuropsychological services; specific supplementary guidelines require at least 50% of those clinical services to involve integrative assessment. The overview also states that services must be integrative. Verify these requirements through application review; they cannot be reduced to a uniform duration for every position. Verify state licensing supervised-hour requirements separately.

questions.answer: Repetitive standardized administration, extended report writing, judgment pressure involving high-risk populations, and long-term supervision and certification maintenance requirements.
